The '''2002–03 season''' was [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]'s 89th competitive season, 11th consecutive season in the [[Premier League]] and 97th year as a club. The club was managed by [[Claudio Ranieri]].

In the [[2002–03 FA Premier League|Premier League]], Chelsea finished fourth behind [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]], [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] and [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]]. With the fourth-place finish, Chelsea secured a place in the [[2003–04 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League third qualifying round]].

In the [[2002–03 UEFA Cup|UEFA Cup]], Chelsea took a first round exit, losing 5–4 on aggregate to [[Norway|Norwegian]] club [[Viking FK|Viking]]. Chelsea also managed to reach the quarter-finals of both the [[2002–03 Football League Cup|Football League Cup]] and the [[2002–03 FA Cup|FA Cup]], but lost 1–0 to [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] and 3–1 to [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] in a replay, respectively.

==Team kit==
The team kit was produced by [[Umbro]]. The shirt sponsor was the airline [[Emirates (airline)|Emirates]]; the kit bore the "Fly Emirates" logo. Chelsea's home kit (all blue with a white trimmed collar) was carried over from the previous campaign. Their new away kit was all black with blue accents. The club's third kit for this season was the club's away kit from the previous season, all white with blue socks and accents.
